evidence.title: Authorization errors over the line
evidence.body: 27% of payment authorizations fail. The pager fires at 20%.

evidence.title: Retries pile on
evidence.body: Rejected sessions retry on their own — 140 retries a second hit the gateway.

evidence.title: The verifier rejects new sessions
evidence.body: token verifier: unknown key identifier on newly issued sessions

evidence.title: Failed authorization trace
evidence.body: The issuer signs new sessions with K72, but the verifier that checks those signatures still accepts only K71.

evidence.title: Platform key-set comparison
evidence.body: Sam's War Room report confirms that the verifier still accepts K71.

evidence.title: Deployment comparison
evidence.body: Build 1847 switched issuer keys before the verifier key set was ready.

evidence.title: Unattributed deployment annotation
evidence.body: A transient UNKNOWN annotation links build 1847 to an unexplained change notice.

beats.narrate: Two nights later. The pager is louder than you remember.

beats.speaker: PAGER
beats.text: SEV1 · Payment Gateway · authorization errors above 20%

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: The checkout alert is real. We still need to separate issuer failures from gateway load.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: By the way — your 02:23 line. I grepped every test harness we own. None of them writes "Good."

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Security closed your log-line ticket, by the way. "No owner found." That was the whole reply.

beats.narrate: The 02:23 line is still in a text file on your desktop. You haven't told anyone.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Customers report failed payments. We can't tell yet whether retries also succeed.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Identity build 1847 went out an hour ago. Everyone will want to roll it back. Let's know why first.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Sam from Platform is on the bridge tonight. You can hand him work.

options.text: Trace one failed authorization end to end

beats.log: token verifier: unknown key identifier on newly issued sessions
trace auth-7731: issuer kid=K72 → verifier accepts [K71] → reject

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: The issuer and the verifier disagree about the key. That's not load.

options.text: Ask Sam to check the verifier's key set while you watch the metrics
options.consequence: Shares the load · Sam owns that part

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: On it. I'll compare the verifier key set with the active issuer. Two minutes.

beats.narrate: Two minutes of watching a retry graph climb.

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Verifier still accepts K71. The issuer is already signing with K72.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Good hand-off. That's two people's worth of work in one.

options.text: Route new authorizations to the stable region first
options.consequence: Buys about three minutes · not a fix

beats.narrate: The stable region takes the traffic. For three minutes the graph looks almost normal.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: The window's closing and we still don't know why. Sam?

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Already looking. Verifier still accepts K71. The issuer is signing with K72.

beats.narrate: The deployment diff loads. Build 1846 on the left, 1847 on the right.

beats.log: 1847: issuer.signing_key K71 → K72 · verifier.keyset unchanged (rollout pending)

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: There it is. 1847 switched the issuer to the new key before the verifier had it. Wrong order, not a bad build.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Two ways out. Undo the release, or finish what it started.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: Support queue just doubled. People are retrying their cards over and over.

beats.speaker: JIN
beats.text: An all-night pharmacy says one card in four bounces at the till. I can't tell them when it'll stop.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Out of time. I'm rolling 1847 back.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Issuer's back on K71. The release team will have questions in the morning, but checkout works.

options.text: Have Sam push key K72 to every verifier
options.consequence: Keeps the release · touches every verifier at once

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Pushing the new key set. Verifiers are picking it up… all green.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Release survives. If one verifier had missed that push, we'd be chasing ghosts till sunrise.

options.text: Page the release owner and wait for their call

beats.narrate: The release owner's phone rings out. Twice.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Nobody's coming. I'm rolling it back.

beats.narrate: You open the deployment record to write up the timeline. Under build 1847 there is an annotation nobody on the bridge wrote.

beats.log: UNKNOWN: deployment 1847 isn't what they told you.

beats.narrate: It links to a change notice. The link goes nowhere.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: That's twice now. Next time it happens, show me while it's still on screen.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: Release tooling leaves junk like that sometimes. File it with the rest.

beats.speaker: MAYA
beats.text: The War Room wants a summary before handover.

options.text: Post the full timeline to the War Room, annotation included
options.consequence: Everyone on the bridge sees it

beats.speaker: SAM
beats.text: Huh. Who has write access to release annotations at three in the morning?

options.text: Send the deploy-order finding to the release team and leave the annotation out
options.consequence: Clean and useful · the annotation stays unexplained

options.text: Post the timeline, then chase the dead change-notice link yourself

beats.narrate: The change-notice system says the notice was never filed. Its audit log says someone viewed it at 03:39.
